instructions: Slice the onion thinly. Cut the peppers into thin strips. Mince the garlic. Crack the eggs into a bowl with 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper, and whisk lightly.
Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 tsp salt. Cook for 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and clear.
Add the pepper strips and 1/4 tsp salt. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft and starting to sweeten.
Add the garlic and the smoked paprika. Stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell them.
Add the tomatoes with their juice. Simmer for 8 minutes, until it's thick and most of the liquid has cooked away.
Turn the heat to low. Pour in the eggs.
Fold the eggs slowly through the vegetables with a spatula for 2 to 3 minutes. Take the pan off the heat while they're still creamy and soft.
Chop 1/4 cup of the parsley and scatter it over the top.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: No version had 20 ratings. The lead is Mrs Jones's Kitchen (5.0 from 5 ratings, 3 of them with comments) as the highest-rated that gave amounts; The Simpler Kitchen (4.75 from 4) and Spain on a Fork back it up, and Food Network gives the classic ham-and-croutons version. All agree on onion, sweet peppers and tomatoes cooked down slowly in olive oil, with the eggs stirred in at the end and taken off the heat while soft. They differ on peppers (green only at Food Network, roasted red at Spain on a Fork) and on smoked paprika. This uses a mix of red and green peppers and canned tomatoes, scaled from 2 servings to 4. No ham or bread, to keep it vegetarian and gluten-free.
